osps_ac_01_01_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide: GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation, covering repository write access and private vulnerability reports alike.
osps_ac_02_01_justification: Collaborator permissions are assigned explicitly, never inherited by default: the org repository baseline sets the default repository permission to the lowest privilege, applied and drift-checked as code by settings/repo-baseline.sh. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
osps_ac_03_01_justification: An organisation-level ruleset blocks direct pushes to main: every change must arrive as a pull request and pass required status checks. The rules and their rationale are recorded in docs/rulesets.md and the Monday audit re-checks them for drift. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The organisation ruleset restricts branch deletion on the primary branch, so deleting main is refused rather than confirmed away. Recorded in docs/rulesets.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Least privilege is the default and the explicit setting: the repository baseline sets the workflow token to read-only permissions, and every workflow declares its own minimal `permissions:` block on top of that. A job that specifies nothing therefore gets read, not write. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow declares an explicit `permissions:` block scoped to what that job actually needs, on top of a read-only default set by the repository baseline. The strongest case is enforced by a lint: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may hold `id-token: write`, and lint:capability-boundary fails the build if one ever does.
osps_br_01_01_justification: This repository's workflows take one input, source-attest.yml's `genesis` dispatch string, passed as an action input and never interpolated into a shell; the shared workflows they call validate their own inputs (level.yml accepts only known `tracks:` values). lint:zizmor fails the gate on any template-injection pattern and reports no findings here.
osps_br_01_03_justification: No workflow here that holds `id-token: write` runs code from this tree: scorecard.yml runs only the pinned scorecard action, and source-attest.yml's attest job never checks the repository out. lint:capability-boundary enforces the org rule in the gate and passes here.
osps_br_01_04_justification: The only collaborator-supplied input is source-attest.yml's `genesis` dispatch string, which is passed as an action input rather than into a shell, and the action refuses genesis when a chain link already exists. lint:zizmor fails the gate on any pattern that would interpolate untrusted context into a shell and reports no findings here.
osps_br_02_01_justification: The repository makes no official releases: it has no tags, no GitHub releases, no release.yml and no publish workflow, and .github/workflows/level.yml declares `tracks: source` because nothing is published. Checkpoints are records appended by commit, each identified by its commit id and its own `seq` field (README.md).
osps_br_02_02_justification: No official release is ever created, so there are no release assets to associate with an identifier: no tags, no GitHub releases, no publish workflow (.github/workflows/level.yml declares `tracks: source`).
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS: the repository, its README and its issue tracker are served by GitHub over TLS, and the only download location named (REUSE.toml) is an https URL.
osps_br_03_02_justification: The only distribution channel is the GitHub repository itself, which REUSE.toml names as SPDX-PackageDownloadLocation (https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger). It is cloned over HTTPS or SSH, both cryptographically authenticated; README.md states that a clone is the verification infrastructure.
osps_br_04_01_justification: No official release is ever created, so there is no release changelog to write: no tags, no GitHub releases, no publish workflow (.github/workflows/level.yml declares `tracks: source`).
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependency ingestion is standardised: this repository's only dependencies are GitHub Actions and the canon's shared workflows, ingested by full commit SHA pin (lint:action-pins passes) and updated by Renovate (renovate.json); the toolbelt arrives from the canon at a pinned version (lint:belt-current: v1.67.2).
osps_br_06_01_justification: No official release is ever created, so there is no release to sign. What lands on main is signed instead: .github/workflows/source-attest.yml emits Sigstore keyless source provenance for every push to main and appends it to refs/notes/commits.
osps_br_07_01_justification: GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled on this repository (security_and_analysis), so an unencrypted credential is blocked at push time, and lint:gitleaks scans the full history in the gate ('no leaks found'). Signing is keyless: source-attest.yml mints a Sigstore identity per run rather than holding a key.
osps_br_07_02_justification: docs/continuity.md is the secrets policy in operational form: an asset table naming every credential the project uses, where it is stored, who can reach it, and how it is rotated or recreated — including the one standing token, whose expiry is designed to fail loudly rather than silently under-claim. The policy is short because the architecture removes most secrets: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, and no signing key exists to store. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_do_01_01_justification: README.md documents basic usage: what a checkpoint is, every field of the record, how the head chain is computed, and what a clone lets a third party verify. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger#readme
osps_do_02_01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the repository's issue forms document how to report a defect, and SECURITY.md documents the separate private path for vulnerabilities. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
osps_do_03_01_justification: The project has made no release, so there are no released assets whose integrity and authenticity a user would verify: no tags, no GitHub releases, no publish workflow (.github/workflows/level.yml declares `tracks: source`).
osps_do_03_02_justification: The project has made no release, so there is no release author identity to verify. Commits on main carry Sigstore source provenance from .github/workflows/source-attest.yml instead.
osps_do_04_01_justification: The project has made no release (no tags, no GitHub releases, no publish workflow), so there is no release support scope to state; checkpoints only append and are never superseded.
osps_do_05_01_justification: The project has made no release, so no release or version ever stops receiving security updates.
osps_do_06_01_justification: Documented in two places and deliberately so: docs/tooling-verdicts.md records how a dependency is selected — the priors a tool must meet to enter the belt, and the verdicts on tools considered and declined — and docs/dependency-track.md records how dependencies are obtained, pinned, monitored and triaged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/tooling-verdicts.md
osps_do_07_01_justification: The org CONTRIBUTING.md, inherited as a default community health file, gives the whole sequence: `mise trust && mise install` brings every tool at its pinned version and `mise run ci` runs exactly what CI runs. Nothing here is compiled, and mise.toml declares no further toolchain. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: docs/continuity.md carries an asset table naming who holds each sensitive resource — organisation ownership, the tag-mint App key, registry accounts, the one standing token — and what happens to each if that person is unavailable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, inherited from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file, carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and the maintainer role is held by the @monumental-archive/owners team. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
osps_gv_02_01_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests on this repository are open for public discussion of proposed changes and usage obstacles; both are searchable and individually addressable by URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: open an issue first for anything large, pull requests for small self-contained fixes, Conventional Commits, DCO sign-off, a green `mise run ci`, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md includes a 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: pull request only, a green `mise run ci`, Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects under 72 columns, DCO sign-off, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Escalation and permissions' carries the policy: a collaborator is reviewed before being granted any escalated permission. Concretely, before an account joins @monumental-archive/owners or receives write access anywhere, the maintainer reviews who they are, why the access is needed and what the smallest sufficient grant is - and the grant is then recorded in the settings-as-code baseline so drift is auditable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#escalation-and-permissions
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1 sign-off asserting legal authorisation. The commit-msg hook catches a missing trailer locally and lint:dco fails the gate, with no exemption list — automation signs off too.
osps_le_02_01_justification: CC0-1.0, which the FSF lists as a free licence (a public-domain dedication compatible with the GPL). LICENSE at the root, full text in LICENSES/CC0-1.0.txt. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: No official release is ever created, so there are no released assets to license separately; everything in the repository is CC0-1.0 per REUSE.toml.
osps_le_03_01_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and the full text in LICENSES/CC0-1.0.txt, the REUSE-standard location; api.reuse.software reports the repository compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: No official release is ever created, so there are no released assets; the repository itself carries LICENSE and LICENSES/CC0-1.0.txt.
osps_qa_01_01_justification: Publicly readable at a static URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, for every revision, and the history is public. Beyond that, each revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation, so the record is independently verifiable rather than merely readable.
osps_qa_02_01_justification: Every direct dependency is listed in machine-readable form: each action and shared workflow by full commit SHA in .github/workflows/, and the canon version in lefthook.yml and renovate.json; Renovate parses exactly these. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/tree/main/.github/workflows
osps_qa_02_02_justification: No release has been made and nothing here is compiled: the repository holds checkpoint JSON, workflow stubs and prose, so there is no compiled asset to ship an SBOM with.
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The gate is a required status check on main under an organisation ruleset: a pull request cannot merge red, and direct pushes are blocked entirely, so no commit reaches the primary branch without its checks passing. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The organisation's repositories and their status are documented rather than assumed: docs/migration-playbook.md records which codebases join the governance and how, and the scheduled audit enumerates the live repository population from the GitHub API rather than from a hand-kept list. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/migration-playbook.md
osps_qa_04_02_justification: The project has made no release, and this repository has no subprojects.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable artifacts are committed: the tracked files are checkpoint JSON, Python source, workflow YAML, TOML configuration, licence texts and Markdown, and lint:vendored finds nothing vendored.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: No unreviewable binary artifacts are committed — every tracked file is text and reviewable in a diff.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: Before a commit is accepted, the gate (.github/workflows/ci.yml, required status check ci / ci) runs `mise run test`: the checkpoint verifier over the tree and its table tests.
osps_qa_06_02_justification: The org CONTRIBUTING.md (inherited) states that `mise run ci` locally is exactly the check CI runs and that every change must pass it; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it on every pull request, merge-queue entry and push to main. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions', is the policy and it sits in the contributor-facing documentation: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - a test that fails without the change where a test suite exists, or a lint, audit task or workflow assertion where the product is configuration and policy - and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_07_01_justification: With a single maintainer there is no non-author human approval available, so this is not enforced. It is the headcount wall this project records rather than works around: the same boundary as Gold's two_person_review and SLSA Source L4, tracked as an open issue rather than quietly claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
osps_sa_01_01_justification: docs/release.md specifies the pipeline actor by actor and action by action — what each workflow does, which identity it runs as, what it is permitted to touch — and docs/build-track.md and docs/source-track.md carry the per-track designs. The capability boundary between caller code and the privileged identity is stated explicitly as a design rule. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/release.md
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The project has made no release. Its one external interface, the checkpoint file format, is documented field by field in README.md regardless. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger#what-a-checkpoint-is
osps_sa_03_01_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are written security assessments of this system: they walk the controls, name the most likely and impactful failure modes (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, supply-chain substitution through unpinned dependencies, silent settings drift), and record which are mitigated and which are accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md carry the threat model and attack-surface analysis: the critical paths are named (caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, silent settings drift, forged signer identities in the transparency log), each with the control that protects it and the residual risk accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md is the coordinated disclosure policy and it states the timeframe: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, and what the reporter can expect afterwards. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact and the reporting channel: private vulnerability reporting through the repository's Security tab, with a 14-day acknowledgement commitment. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_03_01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, delivering the report directly to the security contact without public exposure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerability data would be published as GitHub Security Advisories on this repository, with private vulnerability reporting enabled; the org's disclosure policy is SECURITY.md, inherited. No vulnerability in this repository has been discovered to date. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_04_02_justification: The repository ships no software components: its only dependencies are SHA-pinned CI actions and the canon's shared workflows, it carries no dependency track (level.yml: `tracks: source`), and no advisory has affected one of them.
osps_vm_05_01_justification: docs/dependency-track.md defines the thresholds: cargo-deny bans and licence rules are deterministic and fail the gate, sources are restricted to a single registry with unknown-registry and unknown-git denied, and every advisory must exit through an explicit decision rather than being left open. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_05_02_justification: The project makes no release, so there is no point before a release at which SCA violations must be addressed.
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Automatically, on every change: .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml runs on every pull request, Renovate raises updates as advisories land, and .github/workflows/dependencies.yml re-reads the advisory feed every Monday. The policy is the org's, written in docs/dependency-track.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_06_01_justification: SECURITY.md section 'Static analysis policy' defines the remediation threshold, and it is zero: any SAST finding - CodeQL, the lint belt, zizmor and peers - fails the CI gate, and a red gate cannot merge, so findings are remediated or explicitly and reviewably suppressed with a written reason before the change lands. There is no severity triage queue for static findings because there is no state in which one is outstanding on a default branch. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_06_02_justification: Every change is evaluated and blocked on violation: CodeQL (language: actions) runs on this repository under the org's default setup, and the gate runs actionlint, zizmor, the embedded-shell shellcheck pass and gitleaks as a required status check a pull request cannot merge past. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
access_continuity_justification: docs/continuity.md is exactly this document: assets and their recovery paths, a break-glass procedure for the tag-minting App, a succession plan, and an explicit list of deliberate single points of failure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project has no bespoke website: documentation is plain Markdown rendered by GitHub, which is keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly, and the content is text with descriptive link text rather than images carrying meaning.
assurance_case_justification: docs/release.md and docs/slsa-reference.md are the written assurance case, and docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md assess each claim against its evidence: the threat model (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, tampered artifacts), the countermeasures (the capability boundary, SHA pinning with checksums and attestations, keyless signing with transparency-log evidence), and an explicit record of what is NOT claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The gate (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs `mise run test` - the verifier over the real tree, then its table tests, which build throwaway git repositories end to end - on every pull request, merge-queue entry and push to main, and ci / ci is a required status check.
build_common_tools_justification: Nothing here is built: the repository holds checkpoint JSON, workflow stubs and prose, consumed as committed, and mise.toml declares no build task.
build_floss_tools_justification: No build step exists (see the build criterion).
build_preserve_debug_justification: No build or installation system exists.
build_repeatable_justification: No building occurs: there is no release.yml and no publish workflow (the gate reports lint:release-stub 'no release.yml, not a versioned repo'), and .github/workflows/level.yml declares `tracks: source` because nothing is published.
build_reproducible_justification: No building occurs: there is no release.yml and no publish workflow, and level.yml declares `tracks: source` because nothing is published. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/blob/main/.github/workflows/level.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: No native binaries: nothing in this repository is compiled or linked, so there is no compiler or linker invocation to pass CFLAGS or LDFLAGS to.
build_justification: The repository does not require building for use: checkpoint files are read as committed JSON, and mise.toml declares no build task.
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1 — a single maintainer. Recorded plainly in docs/slsa-reference.md as headcount-blocked, with docs/continuity.md carrying the succession and break-glass paths that exist precisely because of it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
code_of_conduct_justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is inherited from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file; GitHub's community profile for this repository links it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Code review' documents how review is conducted and what must be checked: that the change does what it says, that the claim it makes is one its checks actually enforce, that it does not weaken a documented control, and that documentation changed alongside behaviour - with the mechanical floor (formatting, linting, licence headers, commit shape, tests) left to the CI gate rather than the reviewer. What is required to be acceptable is stated too: a green gate, resolved review threads enforced by ruleset, a DCO sign-off on every commit, and a PR title and body fit to become the permanent squash commit. It also records that with one maintainer there is no second human reviewer, and names the gate as the compensating control. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Automatically, in the gate on every pull request: lint:python (ruff check and format), lint:yaml, lint:actions, lint:zizmor, lint:shell-embedded, lint:biome, lint:toml, lint:markdown, lint:typos and lint:editorconfig, with Conventional Commits checked by lint:commits.
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the gate as the coding standard in executable form, and the standards are specific per language: shellcheck for shell (with bash pinned by `[task_config] shell` because Ubuntu's sh is dash), actionlint and zizmor for workflow YAML, rumdl for Markdown, typos for spelling with the locale registers written down, and Conventional Commits with a 72-column subject ceiling. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the process explicitly: fork/branch, conventional imperative commit subjects under 72 columns enforced by committed, DCO sign-off, `mise run ci` green locally, pull request, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: every change arrives by pull request, must pass `mise run ci` (the coding standard in executable form), uses Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects, and is squash-merged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: There is one significant contributor, so there cannot be two unassociated ones. Headcount, not policy: contributions are welcomed under CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
copyright_per_file_justification: Every file carries a copyright statement, attached through REUSE.toml rather than inline - the REUSE specification's supported mechanism. lint:reuse reports 13 of 13 files with copyright information and enforces it in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/blob/main/REUSE.toml
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The project implements no cryptography and selects no algorithms; where cryptography is used it is Sigstore's and GitHub's, whose algorithm choices the project does not control.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptographic operations are delegated to software built for the purpose — Sigstore/cosign, GitHub's attestation tooling and git — never reimplemented here.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Nothing here makes network connections: the one script, verify/verify_chain.py, reads local files and git; the rest is checkpoint data and CI configuration.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The repository stores no authentication credentials or private keys. Its one secret lives in the source-attest environment, never in files, and source attestations are signed with ephemeral Sigstore keys.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography relied on is implementable with FLOSS: Sigstore, cosign and git are open source.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project selects no keylengths: source attestations use ephemeral Sigstore keys with Fulcio-issued certificates, and transport keys belong to GitHub.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software stores no passwords and authenticates no external users.
crypto_pfs_justification: The repository implements no key agreement protocol; its one script reads local files and git, and it is not a network service.
crypto_published_justification: The project implements no cryptography of its own. Where it relies on cryptography it uses published, expert-reviewed mechanisms: Sigstore (Fulcio certificates, Rekor transparency log), GitHub artifact attestations, SHA-256 checksums and OpenPGP-free keyless signing.
crypto_random_justification: The repository generates no cryptographic keys or nonces; source-attestation signing keys are generated by Sigstore.
crypto_tls12_justification: Nothing here makes network connections: the one script, verify/verify_chain.py, reads local files and git; the rest is checkpoint data and CI configuration.
crypto_used_network_justification: Nothing here makes network connections: the one script, verify/verify_chain.py, reads local files and git; the rest is checkpoint data and CI configuration.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Nothing here makes network connections or sends private information: the one script, verify/verify_chain.py, reads local files and git.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Integrity is SHA-256 throughout - the checkpoint Merkle tree and head chain (README.md) and every action pinned by commit SHA - and source attestations are signed with Sigstore's ECDSA P-256. No MD5 or SHA-1 is relied on as a security mechanism.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is depended on for security: the checkpoint chain uses SHA-256 (README.md) and source attestations use Sigstore's ECDSA P-256.
dco_justification: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1: every commit must carry Signed-off-by; the commit-msg hook catches it locally and lint:dco enforces it in this repository's gate, with no exemption list - Renovate signs off too. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
delivery_mitm_justification: Everything is delivered over HTTPS by GitHub. Beyond transport, every uses: in this repository is pinned to a full commit SHA (lint:action-pins), and the toolbelt arrives from the canon at a pinned version with its own checksummed lockfile.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Nothing is fetched by checksum over http: every action is pinned by commit SHA in the workflows, and the toolbelt's checksums travel in the canon's lockfile, fetched at a pinned version over HTTPS.
dependency_monitoring_justification: renovate.json extends the org Renovate preset, which opens update pull requests for every pinned action and canon reference (the chore(deps) and chore(canon) history); .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml reviews dependency changes on every pull request; .github/workflows/dependencies.yml re-reads the advisory feed every Monday.
description_good_justification: README.md opens by stating what the repository is - the public anchor for the Monumental Archive's acts ledger, holding only cryptographic checkpoints - and explains why it exists.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests on this repository: searchable, individually addressable by URL, open to new participants, and archived publicly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/issues
documentation_achievements_justification: The README's generated badge block hyperlinks every achievement the repository holds (gate status, OpenSSF Scorecard, SLSA source level, REUSE) and holds pending ones as comments until earned; fix:badges renders it and lint:badges fails the gate if it drifts. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger#readme
documentation_architecture_justification: README.md documents the structure: one file per sealed period, an RFC 6962 (section 2.1) Merkle tree over the period's act hashes, a head that chains each checkpoint to the previous one, and one checkpoint per commit so the git DAG is a second tamper-evidence layer. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger#what-a-checkpoint-is
documentation_basics_justification: README.md documents what the repository is, what a checkpoint is, why the chain exists and how it is verified.
documentation_current_justification: README.md describes the v1 checkpoint format and the repository as it stands; checkpoints/ holds only .gitkeep while the first checkpoint is unpublished, which the README does not contradict.
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the checkpoint file format, and README.md documents every field (v, seq, prev_head, merkle_root, act_count, last_act_id, head), the Merkle construction and the exact canonical record the head hashes.
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md's Verifying section gives the one command a new user runs from any clone, `python3 verify/verify_chain.py`, and says what it checks and what it cannot. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger#verifying
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/direction.md is the roadmap and it is unusually explicit about what the project will NOT do: a target table naming the level intended on each SLSA track, the claims policy, and the ceilings and why each sits where it does (BuildEnv is L0 by attribution, not by choice: its controls are built, but the signed build-image provenance that would make them a level belongs to producers who do not emit it; Gold-level criteria are not claimed while there is one maintainer). Open items are tracked as issues and the table is the first thing a closing issue updates. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/direction.md
documentation_security_justification: README.md states what users can and cannot expect: tamper evidence through the head chain and the commit DAG, salted payload hashes so no payload or guessable fingerprint enters the repository, and which properties third parties without database access can verify. Reporting follows the org SECURITY.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger#why-it-exists
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis is run, so nothing runs with assertions enabled for one: the repository makes no production release. N/A is not offered for this criterion at passing.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run because no production release is made, so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to fix.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is run: the repository makes no production release (no tags, releases or publish workflow; .github/workflows/level.yml declares `tracks: source`), and no fuzzing exists (lint:fuzz-build reports no fuzz/, skipped). N/A is not offered for this criterion at passing.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The only code is verify/verify_chain.py, in Python, a memory-safe language; the rest is JSON, YAML, TOML and Markdown.
english_justification: All documentation, workflow comments, issues and commit messages in this repository are in English.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been filed in this repository; its only issue is Renovate's Dependency Dashboard, so none is unanswered.
external_dependencies_justification: Every external dependency is listed in machine-readable form: each GitHub Action and shared workflow is pinned by full commit SHA in .github/workflows/, and the canon version in lefthook.yml and renovate.json; Renovate parses exactly these. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/tree/main/.github/workflows
floss_license_justification: Released under CC0-1.0, which the FSF lists as free. LICENSE at the root, full text in LICENSES/CC0-1.0.txt, per-file attribution via REUSE.toml, enforced in the gate by lint:licence and lint:reuse. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: CC0-1.0 is not OSI-approved (the OSI never approved it); it is FSF-free, which meets floss_license. It was chosen at founding for a repository of digests meant to be copied without conditions (REUSE.toml).
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the decision model explicitly rather than aspirationally: one maintainer deciding in the open, significant decisions made in writing and in public before they are implemented (the docs-first standup, recorded as issues and pull requests), declined paths recorded with reasons so they are re-litigated against the record, and a written succession plan. It is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file, so it governs every repository that does not carry its own. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: The project site is the GitHub repository itself, served with key hardening headers - verified against the live URL: strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubdomains; preload, content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; base-uri 'self', x-frame-options: deny, x-content-type-options: nosniff, referrer-policy: no-referrer-when-downgrade. There is no separate website or download site. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger
hardening_justification: Nothing is compiled or released: the one script, verify/verify_chain.py, runs from source on the user's own interpreter, so there are no build-time hardening mechanisms to apply.
implement_secure_design_justification: Least privilege throughout: every workflow defaults to `permissions: {}` or read-only and states its grants per job; source-attest.yml splits the read token and the signing identity into separate jobs and runs no code from this tree; the checkpoint format keeps payloads out entirely by hashing salted payload hashes (README.md).
input_validation_justification: The one input is source-attest.yml's `genesis` dispatch string, passed to the canon action as an input (never into a shell), which refuses genesis when a chain link already exists; lint:zizmor fails the gate on template-injection patterns and reports none here.
installation_common_justification: Nothing is installed: using the repository means cloning it and reading the checkpoint JSON.
installation_development_quick_justifica: Developer setup is `mise trust && mise install`, which brings the pinned toolchain, and `mise run ci` runs exactly the gate (org CONTRIBUTING.md items 1 and 2, inherited); lefthook.yml installs the org hooks. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: Nothing is installed: using the repository means cloning it, so there is no installation system to honour DESTDIR or similar.
interact_justification: The repository page describes the project (README.md) and GitHub surfaces the organisation's inherited CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and SECURITY.md on it; issues and private vulnerability reporting are enabled. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger
interfaces_current_justification: The only APIs used are GitHub Actions; each is pinned to its current release (actions/checkout v7.0.1, ossf/scorecard-action v2.5.0, github/codeql-action v4.39.3, canon v1.67.2), Renovate keeps them current, and lint:action-pins passes in the gate.
internationalization_justification: The repository has no end-user interface: checkpoint JSON, CI configuration and a verifier whose one-line diagnostics are for maintainers and auditors.
know_common_errors_justification: The documented threat reasoning covers the error classes specific to this software: credential exfiltration through untrusted workflow input (enforced by zizmor and the capability-boundary lint), unpinned actions and supply-chain substitution (every uses: pinned to a full commit SHA with checksums and attestations), and secret exposure in logs. See docs/slsa-reference.md and docs/build-assessment.md.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designed and documented the project's security architecture: least privilege in workflows, an explicit capability boundary forbidding id-token: write in any workflow that runs caller-supplied code, keyless trusted publishing instead of long-lived tokens, and SLSA Build/Source/Dependency track conformance with written assurance in docs/slsa-reference.md and docs/release.md.
license_location_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and LICENSES/CC0-1.0.txt in the REUSE-standard location; api.reuse.software reports the repository compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/blob/main/LICENSE
license_per_file_justification: Every file carries an SPDX licence statement (CC0-1.0) through REUSE.toml, with the full text in LICENSES/CC0-1.0.txt. lint:reuse reports 13 of 13 files with licence information and api.reuse.software reports the repository compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/blob/main/REUSE.toml
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: canon, Renovate and level pull requests merged on 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15 alone (#20, #21, #22, #24, #25), and the Monday audit re-checks the repository on a schedule.
maintenance_or_update_justification: There are no versions to maintain in parallel: the chain only appends, so `git pull` on any clone is the whole upgrade path, and every older checkpoint stays in place and verifiable.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is committed: secret scanning with push protection is enabled on this repository and lint:gitleaks scans the full history in the gate ('no leaks found'). The one secret, SOURCE_RULES_TOKEN, lives in the source-attest environment, never in the tree.
regression_tests_added50_justification: No bugs have been fixed: the history since genesis on 2026-08-08 contains no fix: commit, only feat, docs, ci and chore changes.
release_notes_justification: No releases are made: no tags, no GitHub releases, no publish workflow; .github/workflows/level.yml declares `tracks: source` because nothing is published.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No releases are made, so there are no release notes to carry vulnerability fixes.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands as a pull request with its own commits; the repository contains the full development history, not only released states.
repo_track_justification: Git records author, committer, timestamp and diff for every change; history is protected by org rulesets and every revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation (SLSA Source L3).
report_archive_justification: The issue tracker is public, permanently archived and searchable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_process_justification: Bug reports are submitted through GitHub Issues on this repository, using the organisation's inherited issue forms; SUPPORT.md states where to ask. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been filed in this repository; its only issue is Renovate's Dependency Dashboard, so there is no unacknowledged report.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues, used for every individual issue. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/issues
require_2FA_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide — GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation — so it covers pushing to the repository and access to private vulnerability reports alike.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, inherited as a default community health file, carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming maintainer/owner, contributor and automation and what each is responsible for; the maintainer role is the @monumental-archive/owners team. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
secure_2FA_justification: The 2FA in use is cryptographic rather than SMS-based: GitHub's supported second factors here are TOTP and WebAuthn, and the organisation's requirement is satisfied without SMS.
security_review_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are security reviews written against this project's own security requirements and boundary, control by control, and docs/slsa-reference.md records what is claimed and what is deliberately not. They are current, not historical: the scheduled audit re-checks the claims they rest on. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
signed_releases_justification: No releases are made. Pushes to main are signed instead: .github/workflows/source-attest.yml emits Sigstore keyless source provenance for every push and appends it to refs/notes/commits.
sites_https_justification: The repository and its documentation are served by GitHub over HTTPS; there is no separate project website.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub; the project stores no passwords of its own.
small_tasks_justification: No open issue in this repository is labelled 'good first issue'; the only open issue is Renovate's Dependency Dashboard.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: zizmor scans every workflow for template injection, excessive permissions, credential persistence and unpinned actions, and CodeQL (language: actions) runs under the org's default setup; both run on every change.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed before merge — the gate blocks the pull request, so no finding of medium or higher severity has ever reached main unaddressed.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (language: actions) runs on this repository under the org's default setup, and the gate runs ruff over the Python verifier, actionlint and zizmor over every workflow and shellcheck over every embedded run: block, on every pull request.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every commit: the gate runs on every pull request and every push to main, and a scheduled Monday audit re-runs the network-dependent checks.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: coverage.py, through the belt's python coverage leg, measures verify/verify_chain.py in the gate's own test run; .coverage-floor holds one derived floor per leg (python 81.6, python-branches 72.0) and coverage:check fails the gate if a leg falls below its floor, with no line excluded. Branch coverage measured at 74.1%, below the 80% bar.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: Every change arrives by pull request and the gate runs on each pull request, merge-queue entry and push to main, including the `test` task (the checkpoint verifier and its tests). https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_invocation_justification: `mise run test`, the org's standard task name that the belt's `ci` collects, and underneath it Python's standard `python3 -m unittest discover --start-directory verify --pattern "test_*.py"`. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/blob/main/mise.toml
test_most_justification: Not measured: the tests cover each property the verifier exists to hold and both green paths, but no tool measures the verifier's coverage (the belt's coverage legs are Rust and Go, and coverage:check reports 'no .coverage-floor, skipped').
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' item 3, is the formal written policy: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - a test that fails without the change where a test suite exists, and a lint, audit task or workflow assertion in configuration and policy repositories. It is stated as policy: the gate's checks are the specification, and functionality nothing enforces is functionality the next change may silently remove. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_policy_justification: The org CONTRIBUTING.md, inherited as a default community health file, makes it policy (item 3): a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it, and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced it. Here that means a case in verify/test_verify_chain.py, which `mise run test` runs in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: coverage.py, through the belt's python coverage leg, measures verify/verify_chain.py in the gate's own test run; .coverage-floor holds one derived floor per leg (python 81.6, python-branches 72.0) and coverage:check fails the gate if a leg falls below its floor, with no line excluded. Statement coverage measured at 83.6%, above the 80% bar.
test_statement_coverage90_justification: coverage.py, through the belt's python coverage leg, measures verify/verify_chain.py in the gate's own test run; .coverage-floor holds one derived floor per leg (python 81.6, python-branches 72.0) and coverage:check fails the gate if a leg falls below its floor, with no line excluded. Statement coverage measured at 83.6%, below the 90% bar.
test_justification: verify/verify_chain.py verifies the published checkpoint chain and verify/test_verify_chain.py is its table-test suite (stdlib unittest, one exact message per broken property), both CC0-1.0 in this public repository. `mise run test` runs the verifier over the tree and then the suite, and the gate collects that task on every change. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-ledger/tree/main/verify
tests_are_added_justification: The most recent major change, the checkpoint-chain verifier (#27), shipped with its tests: verify/test_verify_chain.py asserts the exact message for a wrong head, a broken prev_head, a seq gap, an extra field, a changed earlier checkpoint and a deleted one, as the org CONTRIBUTING.md item 3 requires.
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy is stated in the documented instructions for change proposals themselves: CONTRIBUTING.md, item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' - a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it, and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: With a single maintainer, no proposed modification is reviewed by a person other than its author. This is the Source L4 and Gold boundary for this project and is recorded as headcount-blocked in docs/slsa-reference.md; it is watched as an issue rather than papered over. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
updateable_reused_components_justificati: The reused components are the SHA-pinned actions and the canon's shared workflows; Renovate (renovate.json) proposes their updates and they land routinely, for example #24 (canon v1.67.1) and #16 (github/codeql-action v4.39.3).
version_semver_justification: No releases are made; checkpoints are identified by commit id and `seq`, not by semantic versions.
version_tags_signed_justification: The repository has no tags to sign. Pushes to main are source-attested by .github/workflows/source-attest.yml instead.
version_tags_justification: The repository has no tags; nothing is released.
version_unique_justification: Each checkpoint is one commit, uniquely identified by its git commit id and by its monotonic `seq` field (README.md); the criterion accepts commit ids as version identifiers. Nothing else is released.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been identified in this repository; dependency-review runs on every pull request and Renovate keeps every pin current.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity; dependency-review runs on every pull request, Renovate keeps every pin current and the Monday audit re-reads the advisory feed.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit. SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters who do not request anonymity.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, so reports stay private until an advisory is published. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md publishes the process: private reporting through the repository's Security tab. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months, so there is no response time to report. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgement within 14 days.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process end to end: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, what to expect afterwards, and the scope. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: The gate fails on any linter finding and the org ruleset requires it green before merge, so no finding reaches main; main's latest gate run (43742222137) is clean.
warnings_justification: The gate runs the org belt's linters over everything tracked here: lint:python (ruff, every rule plus preview), lint:yaml, lint:actions and lint:zizmor on workflows, lint:biome on JSON, lint:toml, lint:markdown, lint:reuse, lint:typos and lint:gitleaks.
warnings_strict_justification: Every belt linter that applies here fails the gate on a finding, with no warn-only mode; the one suppression is an inline, justified zizmor ignore in .github/workflows/level.yml.
achieve_passing_justification: Project 16736 was created on 2026-11-15 at 0%; the passing badge has not been achieved yet.
